_about: Fidelity-guard thresholds. Each entry is {value, why}. 'review' means a person should listen before the render is trusted; 'fail' means the render must not be presented as faithful. Values are starting points from the standards and the literature cited in docs/decisions/0011-guard-report.md, to be tuned by listening.

alignment_review_ms.why: A delay under 1 ms between the original and the render is below the precedence-effect window and inaudible in an A/B switch with a 30 ms crossfade.

alignment_fail_ms.why: Above about 5 ms an A/B switch is heard as a flam on transients.

loudness_review_lu.why: EBU R128 allows +/-1 LU tolerance for live programme; a louder render wins an A/B on loudness alone, so the bench holds the match to that.

loudness_fail_lu.why: 2 LU is a clearly audible level step; the comparison would no longer be fair.

true_peak_fail_dbtp.why: Above about 0 dBTP the reconstructed waveform clips in the converter or in a lossy encoder; -0.1 leaves a small margin for players that resample.

timbre_review_db.why: Per 1/3-octave band long-term deviation; about 1 to 2 dB broad-band tilts are just noticeable, 3 dB in one band is a clear colour change worth listening for.

timbre_fail_db.why: A 6 dB change in a 1/3-octave band rewrites the tone of the record.

downmix_review_db.why: The mid (L+R) of the render should keep the original's balance in the three broad bands; a 2 dB broad-band shift in the mono fold is audible on a phone speaker.

mono_cancel_review_db.why: Extra loss of the mono sum compared with the original; -3 dB is what fully decorrelating a correlated pair costs, so beyond it the render has more anti-phase content than any decorrelator needs.

low_end_corr_review.why: Below 120 Hz the render must be the original's bass. A correlation of 0.95 between the two low ends allows the crossover's small phase difference; less means the bass was altered.

low_end_corr_fail.why: Below 0.8 the bass line is audibly different from the record.

low_end_level_review_db.why: Bass level change below 120 Hz; 1.5 dB is about the just-noticeable difference for low-frequency level.

clip_run_samples.why: Three or more consecutive full-scale samples is the usual definition of a clipped run in mastering meters; one sample at full scale can be a legitimate peak.

clip_level.why: Samples at or above -0.01 dBFS count towards a clipped run.

dropout_drop_db.why: A band that falls more than 15 dB below the original for a while is heard as a hole in the spectrum (musical masking cannot hide it).

dropout_min_ms.why: Shorter gaps are below the temporal integration of loudness and are rarely noticed.

dropout_floor_db.why: Only bands within 45 dB of the loudest band in the same frame are checked, so quiet bands do not raise false alarms.

pre_echo_excess_db.why: Energy before a transient that is 8 dB above the original's is heard as a pre-echo; backward masking hides about 20 ms of weaker energy, so the window is 20 ms.

pre_echo_audible_db.why: Pre-echo energy more than 30 dB below the transient is masked.

musical_noise_ratio.why: Isolated spectral peaks (birdies) per second more than three times the original's density, in a one-second window.

musical_noise_min_per_s.why: Below about 40 isolated peaks per second above 1 kHz the specks are inaudible under music.
